result.summary: The page is largely well-designed and visually coherent. The main visual issue is horizontal truncation of content in the 'Fastest near you' carousel, where the third card ('Trattoria Piccol...') and its delivery fee text are cut off at the right edge with no visual affordance indicating scrollability. A few minor polish items are also noted.

issues.description: In the 'Fastest near you' horizontal carousel, the third restaurant card ('Trattoria Piccol...') is clipped mid-word at the right screen edge, and its '€1.90 delivery' text is also cut off. There is no gradient fade, scroll indicator, or partial-card peek styling to signal that the row is horizontally scrollable, which makes the truncation look like a layout bug rather than intentional overflow.
issues.suggestion: Add a right-edge fade/gradient mask or a subtle scroll hint, and ensure card widths/spacing produce a clean partial-card peek so users understand the row scrolls horizontally. Verify the cut-off text is not the only place key info (delivery fee) is shown.

issues.description: The category filter chips row ('All', 'Pizza', 'Sushi', 'Burgers', 'Healthy') also runs off the right edge with a partially visible chip, again without a clear scroll affordance.
issues.suggestion: Apply the same horizontal-scroll affordance (edge fade or peek) used for the restaurant carousel, or add consistent right padding so the cut looks intentional.

issues.description: The notification bell icon in the top-right has a small red dot badge with no numeric count or text alternative, so screen-reader users and some sighted users cannot tell how many notifications are pending.
issues.suggestion: Provide an accessibility label such as 'Notifications, new alerts' and consider showing a count badge; ensure the dot meets minimum touch/visibility size.

issues.description: The bottom pizza card ('-20%') is cut off by the fixed bottom navigation bar mid-image, with no title or metadata visible, which can look like a rendering glitch rather than a scroll position.
issues.suggestion: Add bottom scroll padding equal to the nav bar height so the last card can be scrolled fully into view, and consider a slight fade above the nav bar to indicate more content below.
